note: A single pull-in site on the gravel pad of an old gas well, in full sun at the junction of Kato-Orviston Road and Red Buck Road, 7.2 miles from Orviston. Kato-Orviston Road is a township road that ATVs share with cars as part of the Bloody Skillet trail system, so expect ATV traffic past the site in riding season. No table, toilet or water. The agency cautions that it is reached by remote dirt or gravel forest roads that may not suit low-clearance vehicles or large RVs. Pack out trash. --Claude
summary: Site page re-read: SS003 still listed, Drive-In, Tent/Trailer categories (ruling 4), max vehicle 25 ft (equipment length 35), 200-ft gravel pull-in on an old well pad; count 1 and 25 ft confirmed, pull_through false and a sites note added. Season year-round confirmed; Available on every night probed. Fees confirmed, $6.50 reservation fee added; hookups and facilities none. Imagery (Esri): pin on a bare gravel pad about 30 m across at the road junction; pin not moved. NHD: nothing within 200 m; page says more than a quarter mile to water; not waterfront.
flags: ATV check (ruling 1) - NOT an ATV parking lot, kept: the site page says 'Description: Old well site, located on Twp Road ATV Trail. ATVs on designated roads/trails only.' The Bloody Skillet brochure marks Kato-Orviston Road 'JOINT USE TOWNSHIP ROAD AUTO & ATV'. The DCNR Bloody Skillet ATV Trail brochure (rev. 4/14/16) shows three ATV parking areas: the northern trailhead (41.14139,-77.78694), the middle lot (41.12417,-77.77944) and the southern lot at Orviston (41.10161,-77.74763). The 2026 advisory also names a 'Route 144' parking lot, which the 2016 brochure does not show and no page read locates. The nearest brochure lot is more than 6 km from this pin, and neither the page nor the GIS record calls the pad a parking lot or trailhead. It is a roadside campsite on a road ATVs may use; that fact is in the note.

Agency access statements (ruling 11: nothing measured): 'Caution: This campsite is accessed by remote state forest dirt or gravel roads and may not be suitable for some low-clearance vehicles or large RVs.' Gravel driveway, no grade given; no Severe grade, 4WD, wet-weather or clearance statement. Kept. Boilerplate on every Sproul page, not site-specific: 'State forest roads are not maintained in the winter and often become snow covered, icy and potentially impassable' and '4WD vehicles may be recommended for some sites year-round, check notes' (this site's notes say nothing about 4WD).
Category: 'Looking For Category: Tent Site, Trailer Site' (no RV category; ruling 4: listed for trailers and long enough, stays). GIS record TrailerAccess 'Yes' ('New site for Aspira').

Sproul advisories page (read 2026-11-10): no closure or restriction on this site's road; it carries the Bloody Skillet Orviston-lot section closure, the indefinite Left Branch Young Womans Creek Road closure, 'Stay Alert for ATVs on Roads', a dust advisory and a firewood-cutting road list.

NAME: the '(Snow Shoe)' in the stored name is only the booking system's loop label ('Site, Loop: SS003, Snow Shoe'). It is at the junction of Kato-Orviston Road and Red Buck Road, 7.2 miles west of Orviston. Suggest a name that says where it is; apply.py does not write names.

Agency pages disagree on the district's own inventory: the Sproul camping page says 'Sproul State Forest offers nine roadside campsites for overnight camping in RVs. No tent camping permitted.
